title: Wharfline routing RT pilot scratchpad
content:
Meeting / Call notes (02/18/2025) - initial intake with Wharfline Logistics

Attendees: Wharfline: Samir Patel (CTO), Elena Morales (Head of Fleet), Ravi Iyer (Platform). Redwood: Priya Anand (SE), Marco Ruiz (Solutions Eng), Lydia Chen (Infra).

One-line customer problem: Wharfline wants an LLM-assisted routing decision layer that augments rule-based path planning to handle soft constraints (traffic anomalies, ad-hoc loading priorities, customer-specified delivery preferences) with sub-200ms decision windows at the edge for 100–300 vehicles per region.

Primary goals / success criteria:
- P99 decision latency <= 200ms for per-vehicle reroutes (target 120–150ms ideally).
- Throughput: average 120 req/s per region peak, burst to 400 req/s across region cluster.
- Deterministic, auditable decisions (ability to trace prompt -> model output -> final action).
- Data residency: no raw PII leaves customer VPC; keys in customer KMS/HSM.
- Offline resilience: local fallback for 30+ minutes if connectivity drops.
- Cost target: ~<$0.015 per decision (ballpark; needs refinement).

Current infra notes from customer:
- Edge devices run a small Linux box in each vehicle with a local routing agent (Rust) that publishes telemetry via MQTT -> regional brokers.
- Central platform on AWS (us-west-2, us-east-1). They use EKS for microservices and Postgres for historical telemetry.
- ROS used for some diagnostics on special vehicles (not for routing control).

Key constraints / gotchas called out on the call:
- Intermittent cellular connectivity: windows of 10–40s disconnects.
- Vehicles may have up to 1s jitter in telemetry timestamps; prefer server-side smoothing.
- Safety requirement: model outputs must include confidence score and an explicable rationale snippet. Anything labeled "unsafe" must revert to rule-based planner.
- Legal: customers in EU require data residency; multiple regions needed.
- No third-party telemetry (GPS traces) can be stored longer than 7 days without opt-in.

Initial technical sketch (Redwood + customer hybrid approach):
1) Edge-first decision path: keep a tiny local fallback planner (existing rule-based) on devices. When connected, device calls local regional Redwood Private endpoint (VPC) via MQTT bridge / short HTTP.
2) Redwood Private in customer VPC (preferred) -> hosts a lightweight runtime pinned to a compact model variant for strict latency (e.g., redwood-6B-quantized or equivalent).
3) Smart routing: requests are routed to Dedicated pool for peak traffic, fallback to smaller model hosted in-customer if dedicated capacity constrained. Canary rollouts via Redwood Console (10% traffic -> 30% -> 100%).
4) Caching: prefix/KV caching for repeated route templates, aggressive TTL for route fragments.
5) Batching: maintain continuous batching with 10–25ms micro-batch window; tune per-region.
6) Offline reconciliation: device queues decisions locally; on reconnect, central job reconciles differences and logs audit trail.

Model / runtime recommendations (rough):
- Use a small, latency-optimized model for in-flight decisions (6B quantized) with deterministic decoding (greedy + constrained tokens).
- For periodic heavy analysis (e.g., end-of-shift aggregated re-routing suggestions), use larger model (22B) in non-latency path.
- Strongly recommend 8-bit quantization and kernel tuning on customer GPU SKU.
- Streaming vs single-shot: single-shot per decision preferred (lower overall ops).

Observability / auditability:
- Redwood Console: per-route dashboards, token latency breakdown, and tracing hooks.
- Asset link: every model response must be attached to a decision id and saved (metadata only) to allow 7-day replays; avoid storing raw PII.

Immediate open questions for Wharfline (need answers before we size PoC):
- Exact average tokens per decision (their team guessed 80–150 tokens).
- Peak concurrent vehicles per region during 6–9 AM/5–7 PM windows.
- Acceptable tradeoff on correctness vs latency (is 95% correctness at 150ms acceptable?).
- Which KMS/HSM vendor will be used (AWS KMS vs external HSM)?
- Are there regulatory constraints on GPS traces (region-specific) beyond 7-day TTL?

Risks we flagged internally:
- If model outputs are non-deterministic, safety checks become complex -> need strict decoding and deterministic seeds.
- Edge-initiated calls with high jitter could break batching assumptions.
- Customer GPUs may be older; quantization/ops might not hit planned latency without kernel tuning.

Owner-level next steps (rough timeline):
- (Priya) Draft PoC plan + pricing sketch for Private deployment in VPC with 6B quantized baseline. Due: 2025-02-23.
- (Marco) Quick infra feasibility: MQTT bridge options (EMQX vs brokered HTTP) and sample EKS config. Due: 2025-02-25.
- (Lydia) Latency budgeting exercise: simulated 120 req/s micro-batch with 10ms batch window; confirm p99 estimates on our benchmark infra. Due: 2025-02-27.
- (Wharfline / Samir) Provide token estimate per decision and peak vehicle numbers. Due: 2025-02-24.

Proposed PoC scope (2–4 weeks):
- Deploy Redwood Private (trial image) in Wharfline VPC (single region).
- Wire MQTT -> HTTP bridge, implement authentication using customer KMS keys.
- Use a small model variant for live testing, route 5 vehicles initially (shadow), then 50 for load step.
- Validate latency, offline reconciliation, and canary path to rule-based fallback.

Notes-to-self (fragmented):
- Look up prior EMQX integration doc (internal drive).
- Check if "prefix caching" for route fragments already in runtime (Marco thinks yes).
- Ask infra about a prebuilt 6B quantized image for nv4 vs a100; kernel differences matter.

Action: ping Samir to confirm preferred KMS and GDPR contact. Also schedule 30-min technical deep-dive for 02/26 (confirm with Wharfline).

Microspec snippet to include in PoC: (example prompt + safety wrapper)
- Input: vehicle_state {lat, lon, heading, speed}, nearby_events[], load_priority[], ETA_target
- Prompt: "Given the vehicle_state and constraints, produce a single route delta with confidence (0-1) and a short (<=40 char) reason code. If confidence < 0.6, return 'fallback-rule'"

End of scratchpad. Will iterate after PoC plan + customer answers come in.
